reader.label: Effective little-o bound in the treewidth

sourceBasis.step: For a clique of size ℓ in an n-vertex graph, Lin gives a Set Cover instance with budget ℓ(ℓ−1)/2 and universe size at most g(ℓ) log₂ n for a computable g. Apply the construction of Bodlaender et al. to its incidence graph: join a new vertex to every set vertex and to a private leaf. After rejecting instances with an uncovered element, the graph is connected and bipartite, and its domination budget is k=ℓ(ℓ−1)/2+1. The universe vertices together with the new vertex form a vertex cover, so the treewidth is at most g(ℓ) log₂ n+1. Effective sublinearity therefore bounds the exponential factor by a computable function of ℓ times n, while f(k) depends only on ℓ. The claimed algorithm would thus decide Clique in fixed-parameter time.
